cases.customer_question: How can Bluetooth profile testing be avoided during a re-listing when the product functionality has not changed from an earlier qualified release?
question_variants: Can profile testing be skipped using previous QDIDs?
Can A2DP and other profiles inherit prior qualification?
How to avoid profile test report uploads
Can profile ICS be inherited from earlier products?
Reuse FY23 profile qualification for FY26
Can profile testing be avoided if functionality is unchanged?
cases.actual_issue: The project needed to determine whether existing profile qualifications and ICS declarations from a prior QDID could be inherited to avoid new profile testing and report uploads.
cases.plain_english_explanation: The product still supported the same Bluetooth profile features as an older already qualified version. Instead of running all profile tests again, the consultant evaluated whether the qualification could legally inherit the previous profile behavior. The key condition was that no new profile functionality or ICS support items had been added.
cases.consultant_answer: The consultant proposed including the compatible Subset QDID, the existing subsystem QDID, and the FY23 profile qualification QDID together so that A2DP and other profiles could be inherited at the ICS level. This approach would avoid profile testing and report uploads if the FY26 implementation did not add any new profile support items beyond the FY23 qualification scope. The consultant explicitly recommended preserving the same profile functionality to maintain reuse eligibility.
cases.decision_logic: Bluetooth profile qualification reuse is valid when the implementation and ICS profile support remain functionally identical to the inherited qualified design. Adding new profile capabilities or ICS support items invalidates the reuse assumption and creates new testing obligations.
cases.final_recommendation: Reuse the earlier profile qualification QDID and preserve identical profile ICS functionality so profile testing and report uploads can be avoided.
cases.risk_if_done_wrong: If additional profile functionality exists but is not qualified, the product qualification may become incomplete or invalid. Incorrect profile inheritance could also trigger mandatory profile testing and report upload requirements.
